Recent indicators suggest solid growth and easing—but still elevated—inflation, and the Committee’s 25 bp cut to 4.25–4.50 percent alongside ongoing balance-sheet runoff is consistent with a balanced-risk stance. Insights from the Financial Stability Report reinforce a cautiously constructive outlook: banks’ risk-based capital ratios remain above pre-pandemic levels, high-quality liquid assets and LCR/stress-testing frameworks support resilience, and reliance on uninsured deposits has declined. Market functioning and risk appetite appear orderly (strong non-agency issuance earlier in 2024; hedge fund deleveraging reduced leverage). At the same time, the FSR highlights vulnerabilities that warrant prudence—tightened bank lending standards, exposure to short-term wholesale funding in parts of the system, and tail risks from U.S. fiscal sustainability and geopolitical tensions—all consistent with the Committee’s “roughly balanced” risk assessment. Netting these, the tone remains constructive but measured.
